correctness.rationale: The interpolation nodes and weights are derived symbolically; direct multiplication of the two ratio-specific 2x2 matrices gives trace and determinant depending only on q=r+1/r. The strict degree-two Jury inequalities, proved by three displayed positive polynomials on q>=2, give sharp spectral bound 1/5; the quartic discriminant has exactly one positive root and derivative signs prove the unique optimum. Exact rational and interval program checks corroborate, not replace, proof. Claim excludes arbitrary grids and uniform transient bounds.

value.rationale: Unrestricted fixed-ratio alternating meshes are a natural non-smooth-grid stress test against customary sufficient step-ratio bounds for BDF3. The fully explicit Floquet spectrum, global 1/5 barrier, and unique highly nonuniform optimal damping ratio resolve a structural numerical-stability/design question. Unlike a textbook frozen-coefficient root check, it exploits a noncommuting two-step product to establish all-ratio stability.
